title: GPT-6 Discovers Counterexample Disproving the p-Adic Hodge-Theory C_st Conjecture on Open Discs
whyItMatters: Refutes the rigid-analytic C_st conjecture in p-adic Hodge theory via an explicit GPT-6 counterexample family of elliptic curves over an open disc and a non-Kähler elliptic surface over a 2D polydisc.
summary: Pierre Colmez, Wiesława Nizioł, and Xinyu Shao construct explicit counterexamples to the open-disc rigid-analytic C_st conjecture in p-adic Hodge theory and establish a sharp local criterion for semistable comparison. The authors explicitly credit GPT-6 with discovering the degree-1 counterexample family of elliptic curves over an open disc (Section 3.1) as well as the higher-dimensional non-Kähler elliptic surface counterexample over a two-dimensional polydisc (Section 4.3), while GPT-6, Claude Fable 5.2, and Claude Opus 5.5 assisted in proving the accompanying local criterion.
technicalHighlights: GPT-6 discovered the explicit elliptic curve family over an open p-adic disc violating the C_st conjecture in cohomological degree 1.
GPT-6 also constructed a higher-dimensional non-Kähler elliptic surface counterexample over a 2D polydisc.
Authored by leading p-adic Hodge theorists Pierre Colmez and Wiesława Nizioł (IMJ-PRG / CNRS) with Xinyu Shao, establishing a new local criterion for period maps.
caveats: Released as an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2611.27054) undergoing peer review; proofs are human-written and human-checked rather than formalized in Lean 4.

scoreRationale.foundational: Refutes a central rigid-analytic conjecture in p-adic Hodge theory and clarifies the exact boundary of semistable period-map comparison.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly shapes active research in p-adic geometry, rigid-analytic cohomology, and AI-assisted arithmetic geometry.
scoreRationale.verification: Authored and checked by top domain experts in p-adic Hodge theory, though still an arXiv preprint awaiting journal refereeing.
scoreRationale.velocity: GPT-6 surfaced both the degree-1 and 2D polydisc counterexamples rapidly during active frontier research.
